tips.text: Press Ctrl+B to jump straight to the block search at the top of the Actions toolbox, then type part of a block's name.
Player blocks are one combined block with a Player ID dropdown. The block color follows the Player Sprite ID you pick.
The Convert blocks turn a playfield column or row into the matching Player, Missile or Ball X or Y position, and back again.
The Title tab draws full-screen bitmap pages with the Titlescreen Kernel, typically for a title or menu screen.
The Score tab offers a variety of fonts, as well as tools to make or import your own.
The Text Minikernel shows a message 12 characters wide. Use A-Z, 0-9 and basic punctuation. Up to 2 lines of text are supported.
Data tables are read-only lookup tables of byte values (0-255). Use them for level layouts, spawn patterns, timing and more.
Press Space on the Sound tab to preview the selected sound.
Tick "Use pattern tempo" and set a Tempo (BPM) to change the speed of just one pattern, instead of the whole song.
Turn off "Load last open project on startup" on the Options tab and the app always starts from an empty project.
Emulator Settings (the gear icon) switches between the 6502.ts and gopher2600 emulators and adds TV effects such as scanlines and phosphor glow.
ROM size runs from 2k up to 64k. Bigger sizes provide more room for code, graphics and sound.

Drawing tool hotkeys:
Pencil: B
Eraser: E
Fill: G
Eyedropper: I
Line: L
Rectangle: R
Oval: O

Searching the Generated tab:
Enter: next match
Shift+Enter: previous match
A failed build's error message stays until a build succeeds, and it points to the exact line of generated code the compiler stopped on.
Press Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on a Mac) to search the blocks you have already placed on the workspace. Matches are highlighted.
Click the + button on the Sprites tab to add an animation. The name you give it is what appears in every Animation dropdown.
With per-row playfield colors on, pick a color in the quick palette and drag across a background's row colors to paint several rows at once.
A title page is built from graphic cards: 48x1, 48x2, 96x2, Player sprites, Score and Space. The kernel has 8 copies of each bitmap type, shared by every page.
Switch on "5 score digits" and the leftmost digit is left out so the remaining five are centered. Scores up to 99999 still show in full.
A text message can be up to 240 characters. Longer ones scroll, and the Multiline option word-wraps onto a second line.
Click the icon next to a value to enter it as decimal, binary, hex, a color, or a pick from your title screens, backgrounds, sounds, songs or text.
Switch on Envelope to shape a sound's volume with Attack, Decay, Sustain and Release. You can drag the points on the graph.
In the piano roll, click a cell to place or remove a note and drag a note's right edge to change how long it lasts.
Turn on "Increment on Save" to bump the version number every time you save, writing each save to a new file.
In the keyboard mapping dialog, click a control and then press the new key. Escape cancels.
Expert mode hides the small hint text under fields and switches for a more compact layout.
Hold Shift while dragging a line to snap it to 45 degrees, or a rectangle or oval to make a square or circle.
The Generated tab refreshes when you click Update ROM. Editing blocks does not update it by itself.
Drag the strip along the top of the console to make it taller or shorter.
The "wait [n] frames" block pauses for the given number of video frames. There are about 60 frames per second.
Each frame has a Duration: the number of game frames it is shown before the animation moves on to the next one.
A background that no block ever switches to is left out of the ROM, so unused backgrounds cost nothing.
Call "Draw title screen" every frame for as long as you want the page shown, for example from "Title screen update".
Score Bars 1 and 2 can show health (a solid block growing from the score) or lives (evenly spaced dots).
The "Scroll text" blocks add "every [n] frames" and "wait [n] at limits" fields to control how fast and how long it pauses at each end.
The "Data table bit" block reads one bit of a value, so a single byte can hold 8 true/false flags.
The DIM switch plays every sound and music note at a percentage of its volume. The emulator follows it too.
Mute silences an instrument for the whole song, and Solo silences every other instrument so you can hear one by itself.
The Example Projects button on the Project tab lists projects you can open, with a search box to narrow them down.
The bug icon turns on a debug overlay with the registers, scanlines and CPU use. The list icon picks which variables it shows.
"Mute in-game audio" silences everything the ROM plays while you test, without removing any sound blocks.
Mirror draw horizontally or vertically paints the other side of the graphic as you draw. With both on, all four corners are drawn.
"Every [n] frames, plus [n]" runs its blocks on a power-of-2 interval, with an optional offset, so different jobs can take turns.
Press Play on an animation card to preview it in the emulator without building or changing your ROM.
"Background area is clear" tells you whether every playfield pixel in a rectangle is off, for example to see whether all the bricks are gone.
Give a title graphic a Window height smaller than its frame and it scrolls through its picture, using the scroll blocks.
Score digit blocks read or change a single digit of the score without touching the others.
"Show text ID" picks a message with a number, so a variable can choose which message to show.
Export to .CSV and Import from .CSV move a data table's values in and out of a spreadsheet.
Export bank saves every sound on the tab into one .vcsbnk file. Import bank lets you pick which sounds to bring in.
The target icon makes the visible pattern follow playback as the song moves through its sequence.
The Sound Banks button on the Project tab lists sounds and banks you can import into the open project.
The camera icon saves the emulator picture as a PNG. The full screen icon shows it full screen, and Esc leaves.
"Show remaining CPU cycles as the score" shows roughly how many cycles are left in the frame, white when there is room and red when over budget.

Selection tools pick the cells that Move, Flip and Delete act on:
Rectangle select: M
Circle select: C
Polygon select: P
A "Run once" block only runs the first time it is reached and is skipped every time after.
Drag the grab strip across the top of a frame onto another frame to reorder frames. A bar shows where it will land.
Combine "Find playfield pixel collided with" and "Background Clear pixel" to break exactly the wall pixel a shot hit.
Press the play icon on a title page to test just that page in the emulator without building your whole project.
Pick Custom as the score font to draw the digits yourself. "Use extra glyphs" adds 6 more drawable symbols.
Turn on "Show a scroll cursor" to draw blinking arrows (and an end-of-message icon) next to messages with more than 2 lines.
A data table that no block reads is left out of the ROM entirely, so unused tables cost nothing.
"Play sound [type] with frequency, volume and duration" plays a one-off sound without needing a sound card.

Music playback hotkeys:
Shift+Space: play just the current pattern
Space: play the whole pattern sequence
The Title, Developer, Version and other Project Settings fields are also written as a comment at the top of the generated code.
The ROM capacity panel under the emulator shows how much ROM and how many variables your project uses after each build.
The DPC+ kernel (experimental) adds Players 2 to 9, sound chip audio and per-background playfield row counts.

Image hotkeys:
Shift+E: export the current frame as a PNG
Shift+I: import an image into the graphic
"On even frames" and "On odd frames" run different blocks depending on the current frame, handy for splitting heavy work across two frames.
Turn on per-row sprite colors on the Options tab and every sprite frame gets a color strip, one color per row.
A background can be taller than the screen. Background scroll with "stop at edge" ticked stops cleanly on its first and last row.
A title graphic with several frames animates by itself. Switch on "Play animation once" to make it stop on its last frame.
Tag a sound with the piano icon to make it an Instrument. Only instruments show up in the Music tab's instrument dropdown.
Export song saves a song as a .vcsmus file, and Export song bank saves every song with the instruments they use.
Every saved project includes a screenshot of the emulator, taken after the last successful build.
Save ROM saves the last build as a .bin or .a26 file, named after your project title and version.
On a graphic with row colors, click a quick color to arm it, then click or drag across the row color strip. Alt-click removes a quick color.
Define function creates a reusable block that takes parameters and can return a value. Call it as a statement or inside an expression.
Untick "loop" when you set an animation to make it play once and freeze on its last frame. "When Player animation has finished" then runs.
Press Play on a background card to preview just that background in the emulator, without building your ROM.
"End title screen" stops the Titlescreen Kernel and shows the regular game screen from the next frame on.
The Vol row under the piano roll sets a single note's volume as a percentage of the instrument's base volume.
Drag the emulator pane's left edge to resize it, or use the chevron tab on its edge to hide it and make room for blocks.
Set height resizes a graphic. It can scale the contents to fit and apply the new height to every frame of the animation.
"Change state to" switches between the Title screen, Gameplay and Gameover states. Each state has start and update events.
"Player set width/quantity" gives the player 2 or 3 copies, or doubles or quadruples its size.
Reordering backgrounds renumbers them and updates every block that referred to one by its ID.
A 48-wide title graphic can have a colored area behind its picture, drawn with the playfield, and each animation frame can use a different one.
Distance X and Distance Y between two objects give an always-positive distance, handy for checking whether something is close.
Import animation frames picks several image files at once. Files numbered like walk1.png, walk2.png are ordered by their number.
The Fire block launches a missile or the ball and moves it by itself until it leaves the screen. Set the direction with an angle or a Joystick direction block.
The Joystick Fire block can read a pattern of presses (tapped, double-tapped, and held), counted in frames. 60 frames is one second.
Switch blocks have a "was just switched on" mode that is true for one frame per press, so the blocks under it run once instead of every frame the switch is held.
"Undo last move" reverts a player's position if it collided with the playfield last frame. Place it before the blocks that move the player.
Bounce reflects an object off whatever it just collided with. Call it every frame the collision lasts.
The Seek block moves an object toward a target X/Y and stops on arrival.
Set random seed reseeds the random number generator, so a game does not repeat the same sequence every run.
The Fire block's "check playfield while moving" option moves the object one pixel at a time, so a fast missile cannot jump over a thin playfield pixel.
